title: Runtime: add batching tier labels to metrics + cardinality controls
author: Logan Wright
description: Context: As part of “workload-aware batching defaults” we need per-tier visibility (fast/standard/cost-efficient) for latency/cost. Naively adding `tier` (plus other dimensions like `route`, `model`, `region`, `tenant`) to existing high-volume histograms explodes series count and increases telemetry cost. This PR adds tier labeling in a controlled way and introduces runtime-side cardinality controls so we can safely roll out tiered metrics in Hosted/Dedicated canaries. Summary of changes: (1) Adds `batching_tier` label to a curated set of runtime metrics: request latency histograms, queue/wait metrics, batch size distributions, and token-cost attribution counters. (2) Implements a metrics label policy (allowlist + hashing/normalization + sampling) so high-cardinality dimensions don’t propagate into hot-path metrics. (3) Adds guardrails: metric emission fallback mode (“cardinality clamp”) and self-observability counters that report when labels were dropped/normalized/sampled. (4) Updates tracing spans to include tier as a low-cardinality attribute (not a tag on every child span) to avoid backend blowups. Metrics impacted (new/updated): `runtime.request_latency_ms` (histogram) now optionally includes `batching_tier` with controlled roll-out, `runtime.decode_latency_ms` and `runtime.prefill_latency_ms` similarly updated, `runtime.batch.size_tokens` and `runtime.batch.size_requests` now include `batching_tier`, `runtime.scheduler.queue_depth` includes `batching_tier` only when queue is per-tier (Dedicated), `metering.tokens_generated_total` includes `batching_tier` (counter) for cost views, new: `runtime.metrics.cardinality_clamp_total{metric,reason}` and `runtime.metrics.labels_dropped_total{label,metric}` for diagnosing clamp behavior, new: `runtime.metrics.emission_sample_rate{metric}` (gauge) for backend cost accounting. Cardinality control policy: Tier is always allowed (fixed enum: `fast|standard|cost_efficient|unknown`). Region is allowed (bounded set). Model is allowed only via `model_family` (e.g., llama3, qwen2, mistral) in runtime hot-path; full model id remains in low-rate debug metrics and traces. Route is never emitted on histograms; route-level breakdown is handled in the gateway / control plane metrics. Tenant/customer is never emitted from runtime. When a metric would exceed the configured series budget, we clamp by dropping the highest-risk label(s) (route/model_id/tenant) and increment `cardinality_clamp_total` with a reason code. Config / rollout: Adds `metrics.cardinality_controls.*` runtime config (default enabled in canary env only): `series_budget_per_metric` (default 20k), `hotpath_label_allowlist`, `model_id_mode` (`family|id|off`, default `family`), `debug_metrics_sample_rate` (default 0.01), `clamp_mode` (`drop_labels|disable_metric`, default `drop_labels`). Backwards compatibility: No dashboards depend on tier labels yet; existing metric names are unchanged. New labels are additive and behind `features.tiered_batching_metrics_labels`. Notes: The intent is to let observability-pack dashboards slice by tier without having to ship new metric names, while ensuring we don’t reintroduce past high-cardinality incidents. Testing: Unit tests cover label policy evaluation, clamp reason codes, and ensuring tier label enums are normalized. Load test in staging shows <2% overhead in metrics serialization at p95 CPU for the telemetry exporter. Linked work: ENG-18429 (dashboards/alerts) and ENG-18426 (reason codes) consume these labels; INT-33012 tracks missing tier breakdown in dashboards and should be unblocked once observability-pack is updated.
commits: runtime/metrics: add batching_tier label plumbing + enum normalization
telemetry: implement LabelPolicy allowlist + clamp accounting counters
metering: add tier dimension to tokens_generated_total and cost attribution counters
tracing: attach batching tier at request root span only (avoid span-tag explosion)
tests: add unit tests for clamp reasons + series budget enforcement
docs: internal note on metric dimensions and rollout flag
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we guarantee tier stays low-cardinality even when unknown / experimental tiers show up? Also please document clamp semantics; we’ve been burned by silent label drops. Logan Wright: Added strict normalization to `fast|standard|cost_efficient|unknown` and will reject anything else at parse time; also added `labels_dropped_total` and `cardinality_clamp_total{reason}` so drops are visible. Aisha Bello: For dashboards, we need tier on request latency + queue depth, but route is required for some triage. Are we sure route must be excluded? Logan Wright: Route on histograms is the biggest risk; proposing to keep route breakdown in gateway/control-plane metrics and use traces for drilldown. Added comment + doc note; happy to revisit once series budgets are stable. Julian Moore: The hotpath exporter allocates on each label normalization; can we avoid string copies? Logan Wright: Switched normalization to interned enum strings and precomputed label sets; allocator profile improved in staging run. Nadia Rahman: Metering counters with tier are OK, but please ensure we don’t create `model_id`+`tier` cross product in billing metrics. Logan Wright: Confirmed billing path uses `model_family` only; full `model_id` is limited to debug metrics at 1% sample. Caleb Johnson: Tracing change looks good; please add a note about span attribute placement to avoid future churn. Logan Wright: Added to internal doc and a guard unit test ensuring tier is only on root span. Approvals: Allison Grant ✅, Aisha Bello ✅, Julian Moore ✅, Nadia Rahman ✅.
release_notes: Internal: Tiered batching metrics now support `batching_tier` label (fast/standard/cost_efficient) with runtime-side cardinality controls; canary-only flag `features.tiered_batching_metrics_labels` enables emission. Adds clamp visibility counters to detect label drops and series budget enforcement.
